::: {.callout-note title="Work in progress"}
This optional track adds engineering mathematics and modelling to regular Computer Engineering Technology work. It is locally developed, is not endorsed by a college or university, and does not guarantee admission or postsecondary credit. New assignments and the thermal-process project still require development and classroom testing.
:::

## The pathway

Work through the chapters in order. Each chapter connects mathematics to circuits, computers, programming, measurement, energy, or control. Existing lessons and activities are linked where they are ready.

- [0. Engineering design and communication](#chapter-0-engineering-design-and-communication)
- [1. Engineering calculations](#chapter-1-engineering-calculations)
- [2. Circuit fundamentals](#chapter-2-circuit-fundamentals)
- [3. Linear circuits](#chapter-3-linear-circuits)
- [4. Linear algebra for engineering](#chapter-4-linear-algebra-for-engineering)
- [5. Modelling and optimization](#chapter-5-modelling-and-optimization)
- [6. Material and energy balances](#chapter-6-material-and-energy-balances)
- [7. Engineering laboratory and instrumentation](#chapter-7-engineering-laboratory-and-instrumentation)
- [8. Process dynamics and numerical modelling](#chapter-8-process-dynamics-and-numerical-modelling)
- [9. Digital computation](#chapter-9-digital-computation)
- [10. Mechanics and electromechanical systems](#chapter-10-mechanics-and-electromechanical-systems)
- [11. Control systems](#chapter-11-control-systems)
- [12. Engineering design project](#chapter-12-engineering-design-project)

### Chapter 0: Engineering design and communication

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Assess algebra, units, graphing, estimation, calculator, and technical-writing skills; establish an engineering notebook format. | Engineering work must show the model, assumptions, calculations, checks, and revisions. |

**Subchapters:** Engineering baseline; engineering notebook; assumptions and evidence; technical communication.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Scientific calculator, engineering notebook |
| Software | Spreadsheet or document editor |
| Consumables | Graph paper or notebook paper |
| Student deliverable | Unmarked diagnostic, correction record, learning targets, and notebook setup |
| Teacher note | Use the diagnostic to select review work; do not grade it. |

</details>

### Chapter 1: Engineering calculations

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Use dimensional analysis, engineering notation, significant figures, ratios, rates, estimates, and compound units. | Units and estimates expose impossible results and transfer across engineering disciplines. |

**Subchapters:** Units and dimensions; engineering notation; significant figures; ratios and rates; estimation.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Scientific calculator, ruler, sample component labels |
| Software | Spreadsheet |
| Consumables | Graph paper |
| Start with | [Number Systems, Measurement, Units, and Calculator Skills](../01-number-systems/index.qmd) |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 1: quantity and unit audit |
| References | [[1, Ch. 0]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[27, Ch. 1]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) [[28, Chs. 1, 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

</details>

### Chapter 2: Circuit fundamentals

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Rearrange electrical equations, identify relationships, and apply physical limits to a design. | A mathematically correct answer is useful only when the model and design are physically workable. |

**Subchapters:** Charge; voltage; current; resistance; algebraic models; operating limits.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Scientific calculator; optional breadboard, meter, and low-voltage source |
| Software | Circuit simulator |
| Consumables | Resistors and hookup wire if built physically |
| Start with | [Charge, Voltage, and Current](../02-basic-electronics/01-charge-voltage-current.qmd), [Closed, Open, and Short Circuits](../02-basic-electronics/02-circuits-opens-shorts.qmd), [Ohm's Law](../02-basic-electronics/03-ohms-law.qmd), and the [Basic Circuit Calculations worksheet](https://mrandrewandrade.github.io/assets/TEJ_Basic_Circuit_Calculations_Student_Worksheet.pdf) |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 2: resistive design brief |
| Reference | [[1, Chs. 1, 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) |

</details>

### Chapter 3: Linear circuits

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Derive and apply current, voltage, resistance, and power rules for series, parallel, and mixed circuits. | Circuit rules introduce conservation, equivalent models, and independent verification. |

**Subchapters:** Series circuits; parallel circuits; series-parallel circuits; equivalent resistance; electrical power.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Scientific calculator; optional breadboard, meter, and low-voltage source |
| Software | Circuit simulator |
| Consumables | Resistors and hookup wire |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 3: series-parallel design proof |
| Reference | [[1, Chs. 4–6]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) |

</details>

### Chapter 4: Linear algebra for engineering

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Form, solve, and verify two- and three-variable systems from branch, node, and loop equations. | Coupled equations appear in circuits, structures, processes, controls, and data models. |

**Subchapters:** Systems of linear equations; Kirchhoff's current law; Kirchhoff's voltage law; matrices; residual and power checks.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Scientific calculator |
| Software | Spreadsheet or equation-solving software; circuit simulator |
| Consumables | Graph paper |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 4: branch-current system solved by hand and checked with software |
| References | [[1, Chs. 7, 9]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Chs. 9, 12]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

</details>

### Chapter 5: Modelling and optimization

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Build equivalent models and compare designs using constraints, sensitivity, efficiency, safety, and cost. | Different objectives produce different best designs, so trade-offs must be explicit. |

**Subchapters:** Equivalent models; design variables; objective functions; constraints; sensitivity; trade-offs.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Scientific calculator |
| Software | Spreadsheet and circuit simulator |
| Consumables | No special consumables |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 5: source and load optimization memo |
| References | [[1, Ch. 10]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Chs. 13–16]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

</details>

### Chapter 6: Material and energy balances

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Define a system boundary and model input, output, accumulation, loss, and efficiency. | Material and energy balances connect electrical, mechanical, chemical, and environmental systems. |

**Subchapters:** System boundaries; process variables; material balances; energy balances; accumulation; efficiency.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Protected low-voltage source, meters, temperature sensor, insulated water container, secondary containment |
| Software | Spreadsheet or data-logging software |
| Consumables | Water, paper towel, labels |
| Start with | [Power and Energy](../02-basic-electronics/04-power-energy.qmd) and the [Computer Power and Parts mission](../computer-systems/computer-power-parts.qmd) |
| Student deliverables | Assignment 6: energy audit; Lab 1: supervised low-voltage thermal balance |
| References | [[1, Chs. 1, 12]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[27, Chs. 3, 5–6]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) |

</details>

::: {.callout-important title="Safety boundary"}
Use only teacher-approved protected low-voltage equipment. Students do not construct or probe mains circuits. Isolate liquids from exposed electronics and define temperature, current, containment, and shutdown limits before testing.
:::

### Chapter 7: Engineering laboratory and instrumentation

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Collect repeatable data, fit a model, inspect residuals, and state its range and uncertainty. | Measurements become evidence only when their limits are understood. |

**Subchapters:** Measurement; sensors and instrumentation; calibration; regression; residuals; uncertainty.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Sensor, reference instrument, data-collection setup |
| Software | Spreadsheet with graphing and regression |
| Consumables | Labels and test samples appropriate to the sensor |
| Student deliverable | Lab 2: sensor calibration and model check |
| References | [[1, Ch. 8]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Chs. 3, 4, 17, 20]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

</details>

### Chapter 8: Process dynamics and numerical modelling

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Model an electrical or thermal system that changes with time using time constants or numerical stepping. | Real systems take time to charge, heat, cool, accelerate, and settle. |

**Subchapters:** Transient response; time constants; dynamic models; numerical stepping; model stability.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Optional resistor-capacitor circuit or thermal test setup |
| Software | Spreadsheet or programming environment; circuit simulator |
| Consumables | Resistors, capacitors, hookup wire, or thermal-test materials |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 7: resistor-capacitor or thermal transient model |
| References | [[1, Chs. 16, 18–22]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) [[28, Ch. 25]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

</details>

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Translate logic, equations, and state behaviour into truth tables, algorithms, programs, and state diagrams. | Digital computation makes models repeatable, testable, and usable in embedded systems. |

**Subchapters:** Boolean logic; truth tables; algorithms; data structures; state machines; testing.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|

| Software | Programming environment and logic or circuit simulator |
| Consumables | Jumper wire, switches, resistors, LEDs if built physically |
| Start with | [Digital Logic and Stable Inputs](../03-digital-logic-inputs/index.qmd) and the [Digital Inputs worksheet](https://mrandrewandrade.github.io/assets/D01_Digital_Inputs_Student_Worksheet.pdf) |
| Student deliverables | Assignment 8: engineering calculation program; Assignment 9: safety state machine |
| Reference | [[28, Ch. 2]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Relate electrical input to torque, speed, motion or flow, mechanical power, efficiency, and limits. | Motors, pumps, fans, and actuators connect electrical and mechanical systems. |

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|

| Software | Spreadsheet or data-logging software |
| Consumables | Hookup wire, connectors, fuses, mounting materials |
| Student deliverable | Lab 3: actuator characterization |
| Reference | [[1, Chs. 13–14]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) |

### Chapter 11: Control systems

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Compare open-loop, on-off, hysteresis, proportional, integral, and derivative control using response evidence. | Feedback manages disturbances but creates trade-offs in speed, error, stability, and safety. |

**Subchapters:** Open-loop control; feedback; process control; response; stability; saturation; safety.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Computer; optional controller, sensor, and actuator setup |
| Software | Control-system simulator, spreadsheet, or programming environment |
| Consumables | Project-specific hookup wire and mounting materials |
| Start with | [Control Systems and Computer Numerical Control](../05-control-systems/index.qmd) and the [Control Methods Comparison handout](https://mrandrewandrade.github.io/assets/C06_Control_Methods_Comparison_Student.pdf) |
| Student deliverable | Assignment 10: control-method comparison |
| References | [[27, Ch. 3]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) [[28, Chs. 16, 20]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) |

</details>

### Chapter 12: Engineering design project

| Learning goal | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| Design, model, build or simulate, program, measure, validate, revise, and explain an instrumented system. | A complete project integrates mathematics, construction, safety, data, programming, and communication. |

**Subchapters:** Requirements; engineering design; prototype; experiment; validation; optimization; technical communication.

<details>
<summary>What is needed</summary>

| Teacher planning | Details |
|---|---|
| Equipment | Computer, protected low-voltage source, controller, sensors, actuator, meters, project-specific test equipment |
| Software | Programming environment, spreadsheet, simulator, documentation tools |
| Consumables | Approved electronic components, hookup wire, connectors, fabrication stock, fasteners |
| Recommended project | Instrumented low-voltage thermal process controller; alternatives may use a motor, pump, battery monitor, controlled fan, tank-level simulator, or renewable-energy demonstrator |
| Student deliverable | Project 1: requirements, model, schematic, build or approved simulation, code, validation, revision, and concise technical report |
| Teacher note | Approve the scope, equipment, safety limits, data use, and shutdown behaviour before construction. |

</details>

## Core references

The textbooks are teacher references. Public activities use original explanations, diagrams, values, and questions.

[[1]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016) **Grob's Basic Electronics, 12th edition** supports electronics, measurement, circuit analysis, energy, electromagnetism, and transient circuits.

[[27]](../../references.qmd#ref-cengel2008) **Çengel, Introduction to Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer, 2nd edition** supports units, energy balances, closed systems, control volumes, heat transfer, and transient thermal behaviour.

[[28]](../../references.qmd#ref-chapra2010) **Chapra and Canale, Numerical Methods for Engineers, 6th edition** supports modelling, error, linear systems, optimization, curve fitting, programming, and numerical time-step models.
